text:
Vishal P: Quick sync — I want to align on a migration/playbook for routing policies + multi-region tenant isolation. We have multiple customer asks (GDPR-heavy, low-latency EU, enterprise isolation) and limited infra cycles. Who can help prioritize launch criteria?

Claire S: +1. Need to know what 'isolation' means for each customer tier. Is it region-only, vnet-level, or dedicated pools?

Mike H: For enterprise customers we usually need VPC + KMS + SLA. Can we map that to our Dedicated vs Private offerings?

Anya R: From product: customers ask for 3 things — data locality, predictable tail latency, and auditability. Prioritize in that order for compliance-heavy, reverse for PLG trials.

Vishal P: Proposed approach: 1) Define policy primitives (region_affinity, tenant_slice, dedicated_pool, fallback_policy). 2) Create a migration playbook with canary steps and automated rollbacks. 3) Draft launch criteria per customer persona. Thoughts?

Jordan L: Love primitives. Suggest we add 'cost_tier' as a policy key so we can route to quantized / smaller models to save costs when SLO allows.

Samir K: Ops concern — if we do tenant_slice or dedicated_pool we need clear capacity billing + autoscale rules. Otherwise SRE paged every spike.

Claire S: Launch criteria proposal (short): - Regional routing tested end-to-end with synthetic traffic - Fallback behaviors validated (cross-region fallback latencies <200ms for EU->US) - Tenant isolation smoke tests (no KV cache bleed) - Billing + quota mapping verified

Vishal P: Good. Also need product acceptance tests for quality regressions when fallback/model variant occurs. Add to infra tests.

Anya R: Customer-driven asks prioritization: 1) Enterprise/legal (high ARR, strict controls) 2) Mid-market (predictable latency) 3) PLG (cost). We'll gate Dedicated/private rollout on (1) and (2) passing.

Jordan L: Implementation note — we can reuse existing smart-routing code but need new policy evaluation order. Example policy DSL:
```
policy {
  match: tenant.tags in ["eu-compliant"]
  action: route(region: "eu-west-1", fallback: "global", slice: "dedicated")
}
```
Keep it small for v1.

infra-bot: Deploy plan created: infra/playbooks/routing-migration/v1 -> canary->scale. Link: https://internal.redwood/infra/playbooks/routing-migration/v1

Samir K: Can we add a one-page runbook for oncall? Steps for rollback, checking KV cache isolation, and how to force route overrides. If something fails, we need safe-fallback to global read-only mode.

Mike H: For rollout phasing: Phase 0 (internal canary), Phase 1 (selected enterprise customers), Phase 2 (region rollout), Phase 3 (PLG opt-in). Each phase requires signoff from SRE/product/security.

Claire S: Risk register quick: - Misrouted tenants exposing data - Capacity double-charges - Latency regressions - Model quality regressions on fallback. Mitigations: policy validation, budget quotas, perf monitoring, evals tied to rollout.

Vishal P: OK action items: 1) Claire & Samir draft launch criteria + runbook by EOD Thu. 2) Jordan & Mike prototype policy DSL + evaluator by next Tue. 3) Anya to draft customer-prioritization doc and gating metrics. 4) infra-bot to provision canary sandbox.

Anya R: I'll also add example customer cases to the doc (EU finance, US healthcare, PLG app) to make acceptance criteria concrete.

Jordan L: I'll keep DSL minimal; no dynamic scripting in v1. Anything more complex is a later PR.

Samir K: Noted. I'll make sure billing/quotas are in the canary checks.

Vishal P: Thanks. If no objections I'll create the roadmap ticket and link these action items. We should avoid scope creep — prefer small, auditable steps. :thumbsup:

Mike H: +1

Claire S: 👍
